name: Colony of Virginia
kicker: Founded at Jamestown in 1607 · England’s first permanent American colony
briefing: The Colony of Virginia began in 1607, when the Virginia Company of London planted a settlement at Jamestown. Tobacco soon made it rich, and in 1619 it gained the first elected assembly in English America, the House of Burgesses, the same year the first recorded enslaved Africans arrived at Point Comfort. Virginia became a royal colony in 1624, and its leaders later helped launch the American Revolution.
answerHtml: Colony of Virginia (or Virginia Colony; do not accept or prompt on “Jamestown”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Governor Alexander Spotswood of this colony sent the naval force that killed the pirate Blackbeard near Ocracoke Island in 1718. Spotswood also led an expedition across the Blue Ridge Mountains whose members were later called the Knights of the Golden Horseshoe.
tossups.r: Its capital by then was Williamsburg. For 10 points, name this English colony whose first permanent settlement was Jamestown.

tossups.p: This colony’s last royal governor, Lord Dunmore, issued a 1775 proclamation promising freedom to enslaved people who left Patriot owners to fight for the British. A year earlier, Dunmore had led a war against the Shawnee that was named for him.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this colony, home of George Washington and Thomas Jefferson, whose first settlement was Jamestown.

tossups.p: In the 1580s, Sir Walter Raleigh named the land later claimed by this colony in honor of Elizabeth I, the “Virgin Queen,” long before any lasting settlement was made there. Raleigh’s own failed colony stood on Roanoke Island, in what is now North Carolina.
tossups.r: John Smith and John Rolfe later lived in this colony. For 10 points, name this English colony founded at Jamestown in 1607.

tossups.p: On July 30, 1619, Governor George Yeardley opened this colony’s first General Assembly inside a church, making it the first elected lawmaking body in English America. Its elected members, two from each of the colony’s settlements, were called burgesses.
tossups.r: That assembly met at Jamestown. For 10 points, name this colony, where the House of Burgesses met.

tossups.p: In late August 1619, the privateer ship _White Lion_ landed at Point Comfort in this colony with “20 and odd” Africans who had been taken from a Portuguese slave ship. They were the first recorded Africans brought to English North America.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this English colony whose House of Burgesses first met that same year at Jamestown.

tossups.p: Nathaniel Bacon led frontier settlers against this colony’s governor, William Berkeley, in a 1676 revolt, partly because Berkeley would not let them attack Native Americans. Bacon’s followers burned the capital, but the revolt fell apart after Bacon died of disease.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this colony whose first settlement, Jamestown, was burned in Bacon’s Rebellion.

tossups.p: Sir Thomas Dale enforced a harsh code called the “Laws Divine, Moral and Martial” in this colony, where settlers could be whipped for missing church. Earlier, the winter of 1609 to 1610 was so terrible that settlers called it the “Starving Time.”
tossups.r: Before that, John Smith had warned settlers that those who would not work would not eat. For 10 points, name this English colony whose first settlement was Jamestown.

tossups.p: The 1609 wreck of the _Sea Venture_ on Bermuda delayed help for this colony. In 1610, its new governor, Lord De La Warr, arrived just as hungry settlers were about to sail home, and a river was later named for him.
tossups.r: John Rolfe survived that shipwreck. For 10 points, name this English colony founded at Jamestown in 1607.

tossups.p: After Opechancanough’s [“oh-puh-CHAN-kuh-noh”] 1622 attack killed about a quarter of this colony’s English settlers, King James I took away the London Company’s charter. In 1624, this colony came under the king’s direct control, with governors chosen by the Crown.
tossups.r: John Smith had once led this colony’s first settlement. For 10 points, name this colony founded at Jamestown in 1607.

tossups.p: The Wren Building at this colony’s College of William & Mary, founded in 1693, is the oldest college building still in use in the United States. In 1699, this colony moved its capital to Middle Plantation, which was renamed Williamsburg.
tossups.r: Its first capital had been Jamestown. For 10 points, name this English colony.

tossups.p: This colony’s headright system gave 50 acres of land for each person whose voyage a settler paid for, so planters brought over thousands of indentured servants. Around 1620, men in this colony used its main crop to pay for the voyages of women who came over as brides.
tossups.r: That crop was tobacco, first grown for export by John Rolfe, the husband of Pocahontas. For 10 points, name this colony.

tossups.p: This colony’s nickname, “the Old Dominion,” supposedly honors its loyalty to the Crown during the English Civil War. George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and Patrick Henry all served in its legislature, which met at Williamsburg after 1699.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this colony, whose House of Burgesses first met at Jamestown in 1619.

tossups.p: King James I’s 1606 charter gave a joint-stock company based in London the right to start this colony, and a second company based in Plymouth, England, the right to settle farther north. The London group sent its first settlers in late 1606.
tossups.r: Those settlers founded Jamestown the next year. For 10 points, name this English colony.

tossups.p: When royal governors shut down this colony’s legislature in 1769 and again in 1774, many of its members met at the Raleigh Tavern in Williamsburg instead. In 1775, Patrick Henry urged this colony to arm itself, declaring, “Give me liberty, or give me death!”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this colony, whose House of Burgesses was the first elected assembly in English America.

tossups.p: Christopher Newport commanded the three ships that carried this colony’s first settlers: the _Susan Constant_, the _Godspeed_, and the _Discovery_. Those settlers first landed at Cape Henry before choosing a site up a river that they named for their king.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this English colony, where John Smith once led the settlement at Jamestown.

clues.t: Founded at Jamestown in 1607, the first permanent English settlement in North America
John Rolfe made tobacco its money crop (around 1612)
Its House of Burgesses (1619) was the first elected assembly in English America
John Smith led its first settlement for a time; Pocahontas, daughter of Powhatan, married John Rolfe
Started by a joint-stock company, the London Company, under King James I’s 1606 charter
August 1619: the _White Lion_ brought the first recorded enslaved Africans to Point Comfort
Became a royal colony in 1624, after the London Company lost its charter
Bacon’s Rebellion (1676): Nathaniel Bacon led frontier settlers against Governor William Berkeley and burned Jamestown
The capital moved from Jamestown to Middle Plantation, renamed Williamsburg, in 1699
The College of William & Mary was founded in 1693, second only to Harvard among colonial colleges
The “Starving Time” (winter of 1609–1610) nearly wiped out its first settlement
Opechancanough’s 1622 attack killed about a quarter of the English colonists
The headright system gave 50 acres for each person whose passage a settler paid, bringing over many indentured servants
Named for Queen Elizabeth I, the “Virgin Queen,” by Sir Walter Raleigh in the 1580s
Governor George Yeardley opened the first General Assembly in Jamestown’s church on July 30, 1619
Christopher Newport commanded the _Susan Constant_, _Godspeed_, and _Discovery_; the settlers first landed at Cape Henry
Sir Thomas Dale’s harsh “Laws Divine, Moral and Martial” (settlers could be whipped for missing church)
After the _Sea Venture_ wrecked on Bermuda (1609), Governor Lord De La Warr arrived in 1610 as settlers were leaving; the Delaware River is named for him
Berkeley would not let frontier settlers attack Native Americans; the revolt collapsed when Bacon died of disease (1676)
Around 1620, men paid for the voyages of brides from England with tobacco
Raleigh’s earlier colony on Roanoke Island (now North Carolina) failed; it became the “Lost Colony”
Nicknamed the “Old Dominion,” supposedly for its loyalty to the Crown during the English Civil War
Governor Alexander Spotswood sent the force that killed Blackbeard (1718) and led the Knights of the Golden Horseshoe over the Blue Ridge
Last royal governor Lord Dunmore promised freedom to enslaved people who fought for the British (1775); Dunmore’s War against the Shawnee (1774)
Patrick Henry: “Give me liberty, or give me death!” (1775); legislators met at the Raleigh Tavern when governors dissolved their assembly
George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and Patrick Henry all served in its House of Burgesses

trap.title: Colony, not Jamestown
trap.body: Jamestown was only the first settlement in the Colony of Virginia. Real answer lines that want the colony say “do not accept or prompt on Jamestown,” so naming the town loses the tossup, even though many clues (John Smith, Pocahontas, the Starving Time, Bacon’s Rebellion) mention it. Don’t be fooled by Virginia Dare, either: the first English child born in the Americas was born in 1587 at Walter Raleigh’s “Lost Colony” of Roanoke, twenty years before Jamestown.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun. “This settlement,” “this fort,” or “this town” means Jamestown; “this colony,” with clues stretching across decades (royal governors, Williamsburg, William & Mary, the 1619 assembly, Patrick Henry), means Virginia. Plymouth (1620, the Pilgrims) and Maryland (1634, the Calverts) are different colonies.
trap.line: Real answer line: Colony of Virginia (do not accept or prompt on “Jamestown”)
